chunks: 1643 - And it is narrated from Abū Baṣīr, who said:
I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “What is upon the Imam concerning zakat?”

So he said: “O Abū Muḥammad, do you not know that the world belongs to the Imam? He places it where he wills and gives it to whom he wills; that is permissible for him from Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Indeed, the Imam never spends a night at all while there is upon his neck a right belonging to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, about which He will question him.”

key_terms.الدُّنْيَا: the world, meaning worldly possessions and resources placed under the Imam’s authority
key_terms.الزَّكَاةِ: zakat, the obligatory alms about which the question is posed
key_terms.الْإِمَامِ: the Imam, the divinely appointed leader being asked about in relation to zakat and authority
key_terms.جَائِزٌ: permissible, indicating divine authorization for the Imam’s disposal of resources
key_terms.حَقٌّ: a right or due owed to Allah, for which the Imam is accountable
key_terms.فِي عُنُقِهِ: upon his neck, meaning as a binding responsibility or obligation

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about the Imam’s authority over wealth and his duty regarding zakat?
ai.summary: This hadith presents the Imam’s divinely sanctioned authority over worldly resources and his discretion in allocating them. At the same time, it emphasizes that the Imam remains fully accountable before Allah, Mighty and Majestic, for the rights entrusted to him. The narration connects authority with responsibility and divine reckoning.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1643 - It is narrated from Abu Basir, who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) "What obligation does the Imam have concerning Zakat?"

Imam (as) replied: "O Abu Muhammad, do you not know that the world belongs to the Imam? He places it wherever he wishes and gives it to whomever he wishes, and this is permissible for him by Allah (swt), the Almighty. The Imam never spends a single night while there remains a right of Allah (swt), the Almighty, upon him without fulfilling it, for Allah (swt) will hold him accountable for it."
